newsitem.title: INDIA: Honda's City to hit Indian roads in November.
newsitem.headline: Honda's City to hit Indian roads in November.

text.p: Japanese car-maker Honda Motor Co will hit the Indian market in November this year with its 1.3-litre-engine City model, the chief of its Indian joint venture said.
"We plan to complete construction of the factory by October. We will start production by November," Teruo Fujisaki, president of Honda Siel Cars India Ltd, told Reuters on Tuesday.
Honda holds 90 percent in Honda Siel and India's Siel Ltd has 10 percent.
But this is a temporary arrangement to help cash-strapped Siel, which has the option to buy back 30 percent by the end of October next year, Fujisaki said.
Honda's City enter a crowded Indian premium car market with models of engine capacity ranging from 1.0 and 1.5 litres.

The sector is already dense with manufacturers like Ford Motor Co and General Motors Corp, France's Peugeot and South Korea's Daewoo Motor Co after India opened up the market under an economic reform programme begun in 1991.
The new entrants have taken on Japan's Suzuki Motor Corp, which has been in India for more than a decade through a joint venture with the Indian government, Maruti Udyog Ltd.
Honda had designed its model, already launched in Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Taiwan, the Philippines and Pakistan, to suit tough Indian conditions, Fujisaki said.
The engine was powerful and economical, Fujisaki said. "Indian roads are bumpy, there are speedbreakers and rains. So to meet this, we developed the suspension system."
Honda has even made heavy-duty horns to suit noisy Indian roads. "India is a horn-please country," said Fujisaki, referring to signs on trucks asking overtaking drivers to sound their horns.

Honda has so far invested 4.0 billion rupees ($111.7 million) in its plant located 50 km (31 miles) from Delhi and expects investment to touch 8.5 billion rupees ($237.4 million) in six or seven years, he said.
Industry officials say premium cars will constitute 30 to 35 percent of India's passenger car market, which is expected to reach 700,000 to 800,000 cars by 2000.
In 1996, that market was 450,000 cars, of which 17-18 percent were premium products, Fujisaki said.
The City would be unveiled for Indian customers next month and its pricing would be decided just before launch, company officials said.
Honda Siel expects to sell 27,000 to 28,000 cars in 1998/99 (April-March), its first financial year after starting production, and plans to earn around 20 billion rupees ($558.7 million) in sales.
The output was expected eventually to attain the full capacity of 30,000 cars per year, Fujisaki said.
"It (the plant) has to go through phased indigenisation," said vice-president N.K. Goila, referring to an Indian government stipulation requiring high local content.
To start with, 40 to 45 percent of the components of Honda's Indian car would be made in India, and the share was expected to touch 75 percent after five years of production, Goila said.
Honda Siel has an authorised capital of 1.8 billion rupees ($50.2 million), which is expected to be paid up by March.
Future products would depend upon emerging market conditions in India, Fujisaki said. "We have to observe the market trend and tastes of the consumer."

Honda expected the government to cut import duty on components and on completely built-up units (CBUs), Fujisaki said. If that happened, Honda would be encouraged to take further steps into the Indian market, he added. ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
